title: One Point Lesson - Positioner Response & Loop Check (OPL-LV-6701-04)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-LV-6701-04 - Positioner Response & Loop Check.

Equipment: LV-6701 (SEPARATOR LEVEL CONTROL VALVE), Discipline: Instrument, Area: 6700 - LP SEPARATOR SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-6701 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-6701.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains positioner response & loop check for LV-6701 (SEPARATOR LEVEL CONTROL VALVE) in the LP SEPARATOR SYSTEM. Poor positioner tuning makes the level controller LIC-6701 hunt and the separator level cycle. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Step the LIC-6701 output and watch the valve response
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Check the ZSL/ZSH-6701 limit-switch feedback
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Tune the positioner gain for a stable, prompt travel
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Confirm there is no overshoot or stiction step
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Verify the valve seats fully at 4 mA (Class IV)
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: LV-6701 not responding to LIC-6701, level control lost | Likely Cause: Stem seized in PTFE packing (over-tightened + fines) | Action: Freed stem, renewed packing, lubricated, re-stroked and calibrated
- Symptom: Positioner giving position error after drift | Likely Cause: Positioner feedback out of calibration | Action: Recalibrated DVC6200, updated firmware, verified travel
- Symptom: Hexane weeping at LV-6701 stem packing | Likely Cause: PTFE V-ring packing worn | Action: Renewed PTFE V-ring packing set, re-torqued gland

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Poor positioner tuning makes the level controller LIC-6701 hunt and the separator level cycle.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-6701: e.g. LSHH-6710 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-6701 before working on LV-6701.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
